FOREWORD This Indian Standard ( Part 9 ) ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 25 October 1989, after the draft finalized by the Methods of Chemical Analysis of Ores, Minerals and Refractories Sectional Committee had been approved by the Metallurgical Engineering Division Council. IS 2000 : 1962 `Methods of chemical analysis of bauxite' covers the determination of different elements in bauxite. This standard was first published in 1962. The committee decided to revise this standard into different parts covexing determination of each element in a separate part, which on publication, would supersede the determination of that element given in IS 2000 : 1962. This part covers determination of magnesium and calcium. The other parts are: Part 1 Part 2 Part 3 Part 4 Part 5 Part 6 Part 7 Part 8 Determination Determination Determination Determination Determination Determination Determination Determination of loss on ignition of silica of alumina of ferric oxide of titania of vanadium of phosphorus pentoxide of manganese

In this part oxalate method for determination of calcium oxide and oxine method for determination of magnesium oxide has been replaced by atomic absorption spectrophotometric method for determination of calcium and magnesium. In reporting the results of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )`.

In a stainless steel beaker, dissolve 1'392 g of silicic acid in 50 ml of NaOH solution ( 5 N ). Warm if necessary to complete dissolution. Transfer to a 500 ml polyethylene volumetric flask, dilute to volume with water and mix. Store in a polyethylene bottle. This solution contains 1 mg Si/ml. Dissolve 26-6 g of lanthanum chloride heptahydrate ( LaC11.7HaO ) in water, dilute to 100 ml and mix. This solution contains 100 mg of La/ml. Into each of the 250 ml volumetric aside, for the preparation of the solutions, pipette the following: 50 ml of aluminium-boric 10 ml of iron solution 10 ml of titania solution 10 ml of silica solution 50 ml of lanthanum solution flasks set calibration

5.3.7.2 Obtain the net absorbance of each calibration solution by subtracting the absorbance of the zero calibration solution ( see 5.3.5 ). Similarly, obtain the net absorbance of the final test solutions by subtracting the absorbance of the diluted blank test solution ( see 5.3.3 ). 5.3.7.3 Prepare a calibration curve the net absorbance values of the solutions against the concentrations of or calcium, expressed as percent MgO CaO ( see 5.3.4 Table 1 ). by plotting calibration magnesium or percent

Fit the burner in accordance with manufacturer's Light nitrous oxide - acetylene instructions. flame. Set the wavelength for magnesium ( 285.2 nm ) and calcium ( 422.7 nm ). After 10 minutes preheating of the burner, adjust fuel and burner to obtain the maximum absorbance. and calibration solution, to Aspirate water establish that the absorbance reading is not drifting and then set the initial reading for water to zero absorbance.

5.3.7

Atomic Absorption Measurements

5.3.7.1 Aspirate the calibration solutions and the final test solutions in order of increasing absorption starting with diluted blank test solution and the zero calibration solution, with the final test solutions being aspirated at the proper point in Aspirate water between each solution the 8eries. and record the readings when stable responses are obtained. Repeat the measurements twice and average the readings.
